## The Trend, Not Just the Number

4 graded seasons on the board. The latest: 68.1% across 1321 games.

When we evaluate any predictive model, the immediate temptation is to zoom in on the headline number—in this case, a 68.1% hit rate over 1321 games. That's a meaningful sample size, large enough to brush aside concerns about small-sample noise, and the accuracy itself sits comfortably above the breakeven threshold for most betting markets. But the single-season snapshot, however robust, tells only part of the story. What we're really after is consistency: does the model maintain its edge year over year, or are we looking at regression artifacts and lucky stretches masquerading as signal? With four graded seasons now in the ledger, we have enough temporal spread to start answering that question with some confidence. The 68.1% figure represents the most recent campaign, a data point that gains interpretive weight only when placed alongside its predecessors. Pattern recognition across multiple seasons is where we separate durable forecasting skill from statistical happenstance.
